outputs.exact_statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and let $f$ be a log-concave probability density on $\mathbb R^m$. Then $$\label{intro:entropy-bound}
 h(f)\ge m+\frac12\log\det\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(f).$$ Equality holds if and only if $f$ is, almost everywhere, the density of $M(E_1,\ldots,E_m)^{\mathsf T}+b$, where $M$ is an invertible real $m\times m$ matrix, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, and the $E_i$ are independent random variables with density $e^{-u}\mathbf1_{\{u\ge0\}}$.

The function $q$ is a smooth increasing bijection from $\mathbb R$ to $(0,\infty)$. Moreover, $$d>0,\qquad 0<q'<1,\qquad q''\ge0,
 \qquad 0<1-qd\le d^2.$$

Let $\mu=e^{-V}dy$ satisfy [tr:smooth-assumptions]. There exists a positive definite symmetric matrix $P$ such that the Brenier map from $\gamma_m$ to $P_\#\mu$ has Jacobian $J_P$ satisfying $$\mathbb E q^{-1}(J_P)=0.$$ The transformed density again satisfies [tr:smooth-assumptions], with possibly different positive constants.

Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and let $\mu=e^{-V}\,\,\mathrm dy$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^m$, where $V\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^m)$ and $c_-I\le D^2V\le c_+I$ for constants $05, and let $A=q^{-1}(J)$ be the resulting Gaussian transport matrix field, so $\mathbb EA=0$. Set $$X_r=\mathbb E(x_rA),\qquad Y=A-\sum_{r=1}^m x_rX_r,\qquad B=\sum_{r=1}^mX_r^2.$$ If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ are the eigenvalues of $B$, then $$\label{mat:strict-remainder} 2h(\mu)-2m-\log\det\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(\mu) \ge \frac1{500}\mathbb E\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(Y^2) +\frac1{1000}\sum_{i=1}^m\omega(\lambda_i).$$ In particular, $$h(\mu)\ge m+\frac12\log\det\mathop{\mathrm{Cov}}(\mu).$$

The sum of the last two terms in [mat:deficit-reduction] is at most $$\begin{aligned} &-\tau(Hp)+\tau\left[T\left(Yh_0+\sum_rX_rM_r\right)\right] \label{mat:expanded-bound}\\ &\quad+\left\|Y(b-\beta)+\sum_rX_rL_r\right\|_S^2 +\|D-\beta g\|_S^2+\gamma^2\tau\left(T\sum_rg_r^2\right)\nonumber\\ &\quad-P_T-2\tau\left([T,b]\sum_rX_rw_r\right) -\tau\left(T\sum_rw_r^tw_r\right).\nonumber \end{aligned}$$ Except for the use of [mat:W-bound], this expansion is exact.

For the matrices $X_r,B,S,T$ in [mat:chaos] and [mat:dual-matrices], any square-integrable symmetric matrix field $b$, and arbitrary square-integrable matrix fields $w_r$, $$\label{mat:commutator-bound} -P_T-2\tau\left([T,b]\sum_rX_rw_r\right) -\tau\left(T\sum_rw_r^tw_r\right) \le\left(1+\frac s8\right)\|w\|^2.$$

Let $A\in L^2(\gamma_m;\operatorname{Sym}_m)$ satisfy $\mathbb EA=0$, and define $X_r,Y,B$ by [mat:chaos] and $S,T,H$ by [mat:dual-matrices]. With the constants [mat:dual-constants], [mat:constants], and [mat:completion-constants], the functions [mat:scalar-functions], and $\rho=\epsilon I+\kappa S/s$, one has $$\label{mat:absorption-inequality} \begin{split} &\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(T-\log S)-\tau(H\rho p) +s\tau\left[Y^2\left((b-\beta)^2+ \frac{\alpha h_0^2}{4(1-\epsilon-\kappa)p}\right)\right]\\ &\hspace{15mm}\le\frac{69}{500}\|Y\|^2 -\frac1{1000}\sum_{i=1}^m\omega(\lambda_i), \end{split}$$ where $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ are the eigenvalues of $B$. All scalar factors in the expected traces are evaluated at $A$.

Let $V:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with $$0<\int_{\mathbb R^m}e^{-V(x)}\,\,\mathrm dx<\infty.$$ Then there are $a>0$ and $b\geq0$ such that $$\label{geo:linear-coercivity}
  V(x)\geq a|x|-b\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^m).$$ In particular, $e^{-V}$ has moments of every order, and $\int |V|e^{-V}<\infty$, where $|V|e^{-V}$ is interpreted as zero when $V=+\infty$.

Let $m\ge1$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be real symmetric $m\times m$ matrices satisfying $$\sum_{r=1}^m X_r^2=I,
  \qquad A(x)=\sum_{r=1}^m x_rX_r.$$ Suppose $F\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^m;\mathbb R^m)$ has weak Jacobian $DF=q(A)$ almost everywhere. Then there are an orthogonal matrix $U$, signs $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\{-1,1\}$, and $w\in\mathbb R^m$ such that $$\label{eq:rigid-map}
  U^{\mathsf T}F(Uy)
  =\bigl(\sigma_i t(\sigma_i y_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^m+w
  \qquad\text{for almost every }y\in\mathbb R^m.$$ In particular, $F_\#\gamma_m$ is an affine image of the product of $m$ mean-one exponential laws, and its covariance matrix is $I$.

For real symmetric matrices $M,N\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$, $$\label{eq:spectral-lipschitz}
  |q(M)-q(N)|_{\mathrm F}\le |M-N|_{\mathrm F}.$$
